I chose the best among them and handed it to Ding You: “Keep this painting safe for me. Give it back to me if I survive this.”

I took the death-faking drug. As I sensed the drug taking effect, I finally learned what was called having more words than what the paper could keep.

Perhaps I shouldn’t have appeared in the Wei kingdom at all. I believe that she would understand what I mean…

That was the only thing I could say that would make her allow Ding You to escort my coffin out of the capital. Otherwise… I really wouldn’t have any chance of survival.

I believed that Jingnü would not lie to me. Since she had promised to settle accounts with those two families, then she would definitely do it. But if I did not mention it in my letter of final words, how would she believe in my resolution to take the poison?

“This will be the last time that I set you up, Jingnü.”

# Chapter 306: To follow through life and death

By the time that I returned to my senses, there were no longer any outsiders in the bedchamber of the Chengchao Palace. Now there was no one but myself and her lifeless body in my arms.

There was also one letter stained with fresh blood. The writing on it had already turned blurry, and it was no longer decipherable.

However, the contents of that latter were now branded into my mind, every single word of it. For all these years of my life, this was the first time that I had ever detested my retentive memory so painfully.

Written characters suddenly felt unfamiliar to me. Those symbols terrified me. It was as if someone was using a pick to carve each stroke of it into my heart, and each chip caused blood to trickle out. It hurt so much that death would be a relief.

I hung my head down to look at Qi Yan in my arms…

She was so quiet, as if she had fallen asleep. There was not the slightest sign of pain on her face. There were still faint blood stains left around her nose and mouth; I supposed that the imperial doctors had already cleaned her face before I came here.

She had changed into the clothes of a common scholar. Her thousand strands of black hair were kept neatly at the top of her head. She did not wear a single accessory on herself.

It’s been such a long time since I had seen her wear such normal clothes. She was the Imperial Husband after all, and the casual clothes of the Imperial Husband were very splendid too.

Now she looked more like the earliest memory I have of her. That scholar who I had stopped on the street, who received a kick from my foot.

I understood her intention for this. She had worn her burial clothes beforehand, as she did not wish for someone to dress her body after her death… Perhaps that included me too.

I did not believe that she had died just like that. I checked her breathing, then I felt for her pulse on her wrist and neck. And then… A cry tore out from the depths of my lungs.

Qiyan Agula, how could you treat me like this.

How wretched of you… That you could bear to abandon me just like that!

I hugged her body tightly. My tears fell onto her face drop after drop. Sounds of crying travelled in from outside the chamber too, but irritation boiled within me as I listened to them. What were they crying for? It’s not like Qi Yan’s dead…

I wanted to make all them shut up, but I just hugged her tighter.

I was crying too, wasn’t I?

Other than crying, I did not know what else I could do now. I was the noble Emperor. The land and the officials submitted to me, but I… did not have the power to revive the dead.

The people of the world respected me. They feared me, they heeded me. But my most beloved person refused to listen to me. She abandoned me, and she used the cruelest method to cut off every possible way back.

The teaching auntie had once taught me: no matter how grieved, the tears of the living must not fall on the remains of the deceased. Otherwise, it would make the soul of the deceased unable to rest in peace.

But I insist. I insist on not letting you ‘rest in peace’! Would this… make the King of Hell refuse to accept you? Would he send you back to the mortal world instead?

‘North Jing History’ was just a book. They were just two worthless subjects. How could that ever be worth the exchange of your life?

Could it be that you used such a method to punish me because I hurt your heart?

Qiyan Agula, say something!

Get up. Argue with me. Make a fuss with me, smash something or hit someone, anything you want. If you had a firm attitude, I would not necessarily disagree! Why did you have to be so stubborn!

You have a proud backbone. You don’t wish to beg on your knees. But I’m your wife, so what if you cried and fussed and made a scene like a woman?

“Agula… I was wrong. I know I’m wrong now. Can you not be so ruthless, to not even give others a chance for mistakes! Can you not be so extreme, to not even give me a chance to redeem myself!”

“Weren’t you the most magnanimous in the past? You never got mad at me no matter how I kicked up a fuss, and you would always coax me instead. Didn’t you say that… You would never really get mad at me, and that you would always stay by my side? Didn’t you say that you would only ever leave once I’ve gotten sick of you first?”

“Yuanjun… I’m begging you, don’t abandon me.”

The sky outside the chamber darkened. It brightened again. It darkened again. I hugged her body that had already cooled thoroughly. My tears have not stopped for a single moment.

Who said that people could not shed tears under extreme grief? Why have my tears not stopped for a single moment? I was in pain. There was not a single spot on my body that was not in pain. But she would not care anymore. She would not coax me in resignation anymore.

Later on, each of my teardrops felt like a ball of fire that burned the frame of my eyes as it spilled over…

I gradually came to accept the reality that she had already left. Because as long as she still had the slightest bit of awareness left, she would absolutely not bear to see me in such suffering.

I was wrong…

I was horrendously wrong, preposterously wrong.

Up until now, we have walked through thirteen springs and autumns together. I thought that I was the one who understood her the most in this world, but I was wrong.

I have never truly walked into her heart. I have never felt her suffering as my own.

If I had truly understood her the way that I thought I did, she would not be lying in my arms without any breath in her body.

I was the one who forced her to her death.

I had only known that she had gone through immense hardships on this road of revenge, but I had overlooked her heart that would rather be a piece of shattered jade than a piece of whole pottery.

I had thought that time could smooth over anything in the world, but she proved to me with her actions that there were some things which could never be worn away.

I had thought that… She was forgiving and magnanimous, and that she would spare Lu Quan and Ding Yi temporarily ‘for the greater picture’. But I had forgotten that this was never her ‘greater picture’. I was the one who used her love for me to force something upon her.

I had always thought that she should get me, and that she should understand me. But I had forgotten to ask her if any of this was what she wanted.

I wasn’t the one who had lost my home and my people. What right did I have to make her step back repeatedly for my sake?

I wanted so badly to follow her just like that. But if I died, the You province would definitely rebel. The north of Luo would also take the opportunity to attack. Then what would happen to the common folks of the world?

Er-jie, Xiao-Die, Yuxiao, and Youhe… What would happen to them?

I was dazed for so long once this thought emerged. Once I returned to my senses, I lowered my head to look at her in my arms. My tears flowed out again, in blood red.

I finally understood why she would choose to leave me with such a method.

I was unfit for her.

She had given all her heart to me, and I had thought that I did the same. Only now did I suddenly realize that that was not the case.

I did not even have the courage to follow her to the yellow springs…

“You’ve already predicted everything, haven’t you?”

I gradually let go of her. I struggled to get up, then I pushed the door open and walked out of the chamber. The blinding sunlight dazed me for a moment. A field of people dressed in white was kneeling outside the chamber. When they saw me come outside, they were taken aback at first, then started to cry sadly.

They were so noisy. I couldn’t quite tell what they were crying about.

I pointed at imperial doctor Wang, Ding You, then Gu Rolan. “All you, come inside.”

The three of them followed me into the inner chamber, then I said to them, “Go and take a look, what’s wrong with the Imperial Husband?”

Imperial doctor Wang dropped to his knees. Ding You and Gu Rolan followed right after him. The pitiful imperial doctor Wang was already very old, he said as his tears poured down: “Your Majesty, please take care of your health. His Highness the Imperial Husband… has already gone into heaven! To cease breathing for seven days and nights, there is absolutely no chance of revival after that. Your Majesty, your Majesty please…”

“I don’t believe it.”

Imperial doctor Wang said, “Your Majesty, this old subject implores your Majesty to prioritize the kingdom. Your health is of the utmost importance!”

“Her body is still soft. There are no signs of decay even when seven days and nights have passed, so she must be lying to me. Go and think of a way to wake her up.”

Hearing this, imperial doctor Wang kneeled at her side. He felt her wrist carefully, then her neck. He pried her eyelid open next. “Your Majesty…”

Ding You replied, “Reporting your Majesty, this humble subject has something to say.”

I looked at Ding You, then I asked coldly, “Are the two of you cooperating to fool me?”

Ding You prostrated on the floor. “This humble subject dares not. This humble subject simply knows why the Imperial Husband’s corpse does not decay.”

“Oh? Go on.”

Ding You said, “The Imperial Husband’s water condition was deeply rooted in her body, that is why the Imperial Husband’s body temperature is lower than the average person. Through many years of being eroded by the water condition, though it had been great suffering… It has caused the Imperial Husband’s remains to decay at a slower rate than the average person.”

Imperial doctor Wang coaxed too, “Your Majesty, it has already been seven days and nights. It is better to lay his Highness in a coffin as soon as possible.”

I fainted again. Before I fainted, I said to Ding You, “If you dared to lie to me, I will definitely make you die in separate pieces…”

I thought that I had slept for a long time, but it had just been four short hours. Once I woke up, I felt as if there was a layer of mesh covering my eyes. Everything appeared indistinct.

I remembered the letter that she wrote before she left. I disregarded the court officials’ opposition to lay her in a thin coffin, and I sent her to the place that she had mentioned in the letter.

I did everything that she had instructed me to in her letter. When the analogging officials remonstrated, I killed the analogging officials. When the literary officials opposed me, I beheaded the literary officials. I fought against the majority to complete all the instructions in her letter.

She said that she wished to be buried in the boundary between Jing and Wei. Alright then… I’ll allow your coffin to leave the capital.

She said that she wished to have never appeared in the Wei kingdom, and that she wished to have died in Jingjia First Year instead. Alright then… I’ll alter history for you and erase all of your traces.

In our thirteen years of marriage, when have you ever been capricious towards me? It was just those two mere tasks, how could I possibly deny your wishes?

It’s just that, do you still remember how many times you had lied to me for the past thirteen years? So why can’t you just lie to me again for this one last thing?

Why?

I visited the Grand General Seignior with a bottle of wine in hand. I ordered the guards to not come inside.

Shangguan Wu was very surprised to see me. He glared at me. “You’d still dare to meet me? Alone?”

As I gazed at him, I remembered da-jie’s passing. I took two cups to the table, then I filled one for him. “Sit, big brother-in-law.”

Shangguan Wu snorted coldly. He refused to sit.

“Qi Yan’s gone. I hope that big brother-in-law could have a drink with me.”

Shangguan Wu was somewhat surprised. He stared at me as if he was affirming the truth of my words, but he ultimately asked in a softer tone, “When did it happen?”

I downed the wine in my cup. Tears of blood flowed out again after that. Shangguan Wu was quite shocked to see it. I drank three cups in one row, then I asked him, “How did you pull through it when da-jie had just left?”

Shangguan Wu sighed after a moment of silence and sat down in front of me.

That night, we talked a lot. A shared experience shortened the distance between us.

I told Shangguan Wu. “My eyes are probably going blind, everything looks indistinct to me recently. I came just to see you.”

What a shame… The imperial doctor still managed to treat me in the end. Although my eyes would feel piercing pain whenever I cried from now on, my sight was still saved in the end.

However, I could no longer read books or look at written words ever again. No matter what I read, Qi Yan’s letter of last words would flash before my eyes… Qiuju took the role of reading out the reports for me at first, and then it was Fu-er…

I told Shangguan Wu. “I will not marry again in this life and this world. I have the intention to crown Fu-er as the Crown Prince.”

Shangguan Wu did not believe it, and I left by myself. Half a year later… I crowned Fu-er as the Crown Prince.

The crowd of officials opposed it. This news travelled into Shangguan Wu’s ears too and sought presence voluntarily.

He said, “I did not expect that your Majesty would follow your word.”

“Would you believe me if I said that I have never plotted to harm you before?”

Shangguan Wu asked, “Then why did your Majesty keep me confined in the capital?”

“I just wanted to reclaim the You province’s military power to the court. I’ve always kept da-jie’s love and kindness in mind; I will not do anything to the You province.”

After that, Shangguan Wu voluntarily returned military power to the court. His son had become the Crown Prince, so he no longer had a need to fear.

But the Crown Prince’s foundation was not stable yet; both Shangguan Wu and I knew why. Shangguan Wu sought me out a few months later, then decided to retire from society by faking his death, which would seal the leisurely mouths of the court officials.

I escorted Shangguan Wu out of the capital. Shangguan Wu told me: once his Highness the Crown Prince grows up, just let him crown Yuxiao as the Crown Prince’s consort. That would count as giving some comfort to his Highness the Imperial Husband.

I shook my head. “Yuanjun did not wish for Yuxiao to be roped into the storm of the imperial family, that was why I passed her on to er-jie’s custody. But if they wished to tie the knot once they’ve grown up, I will not oppose it either.”

Once I had resolved the You province, I dealt with the Lu and Ding families using whatever reason I found.

On the night before their execution, I took a special visit to the prison, and I told them everything.

Lu Quan clung on the prison bars madly as he hurled profanity and curses at me. I looked at him calmly, then I said to him, “If curses worked, both you and Ding Yi would have already died a long time ago.”

It’s just that, she would never return again.

I regret it so much. If I had killed them earlier, she would not have left me.

Once I had done all this, I suddenly missed her so much.

I should go and visit her now. I wanted to tell her that the grudge of the north Jing kingdom had been avenged. I did everything that I had promised to. I wanted to tell her that I have not stopped missing her for a single moment ever since she left.

The south and north were fighting like a raging fire at that time, but I came to the boundary between Jing and Wei despite the court officials’ opposition.

Her resting place was overgrown with weeds, a sight that sliced through my heart.

I ordered everyone to back away. I wanted to clean it up myself.

The weeds had grown too deeply, so the dirt mound was flattened once I had plucked all them out. Hence I put handfuls of soil back on it repeatedly, when suddenly…

The longing that I had suppressed for countless nights could not be held back anymore. There was now a Crown Prince in the court. I wanted to pull her out of there, to make her see me batter myself to death on her coffin, and then jump inside it with the last of my strength, so that I can sleep with her here forever.

You can forget about abandoning me, Qiyan Agula!

I did not wish to let outsiders see what she looked like now, hence I snatched a blade from a guard to open the coffin myself. Who knows how much effort it took for me to finally pry all of its nails out.

I was already prepared. You’ve walked alone on the road to the yellow springs for so long, were you lonely?

Yuanjun, I’m coming…

But the coffin was empty.

I did not dare to believe my eyes. As I looked upon the vacant coffin, I laughed, I cried, I grudged, I hated.

Qiyan Agula!

This time, I’ll find you even if I must search to the ends of the earth!

# Chapter 307: Loss of love hurts no more

In the Guang fishing village of Chiongtai, two huts made of mud bricks and straw stood next to each other in the most secluded corner of the village. It appeared to be one plot because it was surrounded by a bamboo fence, but another bamboo fence lined between the two huts. One plot was segregated into two homes just like that.

There were tall piles of chopped wood in the yard of one of the huts. There were also a few chickens raised there. There was one stone mill, and a simple shack built in the corner of that yard, which appeared to be a kitchen.

A few things that looked like horse dung were placed before the kitchen, fertilizing a few medical herbs. A few washed clothes were hanging on a rope that was tied between two standing logs, and a few strings of dried salted fish were hanging on the wooden posts too. Though this yard looked somewhat crude, it was filled with signs of life.

Meanwhile, it was an entirely different scene on the other side of the bamboo fence. Although it had the exact same style of hut, there was nothing on this side of the courtyard other than weeds. It appeared as if no one had lived here for a long time; it was completely untended.

However, there was a person living inside this hut, behind its shut doors and windows.

It was very dim inside the room. There was only one bed, one chair, one table, and a wooden trunk at the foot of the bed.

One person was sitting on the only chair inside the room. This person was dressed in a long overall that was a washed-out white, and it had patches on its sleeves and lapels. This person also had a men’s hairstyle; kept neatly at the top, secured with a strip of cloth.

This person’s skin was unusually fair. It could be described as a sign of illness, but it was more like a fairness that came about from being indoors for a long time. This person also had a pair of amber-colored eyes, which were now looking at a painting on a wall in a trance.

Who could have thought?

The soulless person in this room was the famous Imperial Husband, who had been wiped away from the annals of history, and the Khagan of the Chengli tribe in the north Jing kingdom— Qiyan Agula. Though the Wei kingdom’s people preferred to say: Qi Yan, Qi Yuanjun.

It was now Chengqi Eighth Year. It had been three years since the Imperial Husband’s passing.

But the Imperial Husband had appeared in Chiongtai, thousands of miles away from the imperial city. The place known as the edge of the earth.

This was the end of heaven and earth; people were rarely able to arrive here even with a decree from the court. The people here relied on the sea for food, and they rarely travelled on land unless there was a need to. It was because they would have to pass through a dark forest that stretched for a hundred miles to the north, and that was why this place was pretty much cut off from the rest of the world.

Three years ago, Imperial Husband Qi Yan took a death-faking drug and escaped with Ding You.

Ding You found records regarding the fire toad in the journals by the Princess from the previous Dynasty: the fire toad was a sort of organism that could only survive in extremely hot lands. The slightest difference in temperature would lead to its death, and its medical properties would disappear too. Throughout the entire mainland of the Wei kingdom, this organism may only be found in the very south end of Chiongtai. As time passed, the fire toad eventually became an organism of legend.

Ding You brought Qi Yan all the way south until they reached this place. The fire toad was caught, then it was used to make medicine. After over a year of nursing, the water condition lurking in Qi Yan’s body was finally dispelled.

But Qi Yan’s mental symptoms did not improve. Qi Yan’s prediction came true: she had forgotten all her past. She became someone with no past and no memory.

She forgot about Nangong Jingnü. She forgot about her identity as the Imperial Husband and the Khagan. She forgot about the debt of blood. She had lost all her memories.

Fortunately, Qi Yan’s behavior had not regressed despite her lack of memories. She still had the same intelligence as she used to have. Her literacy and penmanship was not affected.

In the beginning, Ding You did want to find a way to treat Qi Yan. But firstly, his skill was limited. Secondly, Ding You felt that perhaps this was the best compensation that the old lord in heaven could give to Qi Yan for her lifetime of suffering. Other than making Qi Yan even more quiet and inexpressive than usual, the loss of her memories had not influenced her in any other way. As time went on, Ding You gave up on the idea of treating Qi Yan.

She was still called Qi Yan, because this place was cut off from the world; the villagers here did not know who Qi Yan was. Additionally, ‘Qi’ was a common surname in this fishing village. With this name, she would not get bullied by the locals at least.

Ding You changed his name too. He was now called Qi You. They took the cover of cousins who were settling in this fishing village.

Ding You was responsible for their daily three meals. Qi Yan rarely stepped outside.

Qi Yan gazed at the portrait on the wall. Although it was somewhat yellowed, it was not hard to tell that the scroll was high-quality material. It appeared rather out of place with everything in this room.

Qi Yan did not remember who the person in the painting was. She did not remember that she had painted it herself either, but this painting had an inexplicable allure to Qi Yan. She would often become absorbed as she looked at it, forgetting the time as it passed by her.

Qi Yan had asked Ding You about the origin of this painting too. Ding You told her: this painting was a dream from Qi Yan’s youth. When Qi Yan woke up, she pleaded him to get a brush and ink to paint this person from her dreams.

Qi Yan asked, “Then why can’t I remember it?”

Ding You answered, “We were robbed by mountain bandits. You lost your mind from the shock. Fortunately, we were saved by a kind-hearted and strong man. That strong man said that you have an outstanding appearance; you will easily get preyed upon by evildoers. That’s why I made you dress as a man to hide in this place.”

Qi Yan seemed to have been scared by Ding You’s words, so she continued to dress as a man even when they came to the fishing village. She stubbornly refused to wear women’s clothes, and she would rather bind her chest to wear men’s clothes.

The scars on Qi Yan’s chest were already pretty much recovered. Qi Yan applied the ointment for it on herself. However, she did not remember how she had gotten the scars on her chest in the first place.

This ointment was called ningxiang ointment, which was made from a secret formula Ding You found in the journals of the Princess from the previous Dynasty. It was very effective.

Ding You’s voice travelled in, “It’s time to eat.”

Qi Yan moved her gaze away from the painting and she silently walked out of the door. Sunlight pierced into her eyes at once. Qi Yan frowned as she put her hand over her brows, while her pale skin glowed with an ivory white under the sunlight.

The food table was set at the other side of the fence, along with two stools. Qi Yan picked up her chopsticks and started to eat silently, but she only ate from the dish of dried fish stewed with vegetables that was right in front of her.

Ding You sighed quietly. He tore out a chicken leg and put it in Qi Yan’s bowl. “Don’t just eat the food in front of you.”

“Mm.” Qi Yan nodded obediently. Ever since she had lost her memories, she spoke pitifully little. Their interactions were mostly questions from Ding You and responses from her. Other than her question about the painting, Qi Yan did not voluntarily speak to Ding You for the past three years. She did not inquire about her past either. She simply accepted the blankness of herself indifferently.

Ding You looked at Qi Yan. Even he did not know himself if it was the right thing to bring Qi Yan out by exhausting all his abilities. The person before his eyes was just like an empty shell, and as for her heart… Who knows where it had gone.

Ding You said, “It won’t do for you to be cooped up in the house every day either. It’ll be bad for your health in the long-term.”

Qi Yan replied, “…”

“I’ve discussed it with merchant Li Zheng already. The private school is missing a teacher to teach calligraphy for beginners, so you’ll start work in a few days.”

Qi Yan mused for a moment and said one quiet, “Alright.”

Ding You felt extremely upset to see Qi yan like this… But who wouldn’t?

For the past few years, Ding You had accumulated a pretty good reputation by treating and saving others. Li Zheng specially met with him a few days ago, hence Ding You secured a teacher’s position for Qi Yan.

Ding You had already thought of a convincing argument for Qi Yan’s rejection. He had not expected that she would agree to it just like that.

It was a different scene in the world beyond the dark forest; the female Emperor Nangong Zhenzhen handed governance of the court to the Crown Prince Nangong Fu while she brought a few skilled helpers with her as she went deep into the world of commoners— to travel around in disguise.

Inside the swaying carriage compartment, Qiuju took a look at her master’s thinned face. She opened up a food box at the side, brought out two plates of pastries and placed them before Nangong Jingnü: “Master, have some of these. You have not had a proper meal since we got on the road before daybreak.”

Nangong Jingnü swept a look over the pastries on the table and sighed quietly, “Eat some if you’re hungry, I have no appetite.”

Qiuju asked, “Master, you’ve always been sullen ever since we left Nanyang’s domain. You haven’t eaten properly for consecutive days now. What if you get sick from fatigue?”

Nangong Jingnü muttered, “Qiuju…”

Qiuju said, “This maid is here.”

Nangong Jingnü replied, “Say, where on earth is she hiding in? We’ve already searched through dozens of provincial cities. This world is so vast, if she is sincerely hiding…”

Qiuju poured a cup of water for Nangong Jingnü and answered, “This maid believes that that person would not be so extreme. Didn’t the master say it before? If he had truly ended things with the master, he would have placed a corpse in the coffin… This maid believes that we will definitely find him.”

Nangong Jingnü’s expression finally improved a little. Although she was still fatigued, hope was lit in her heart again.

Nangong Jingnü: Agula, where on earth are you…

Back when Nangong Jingnü found that Qiyan Agula’s coffin was empty, she was stunned on the spot. Once she returned to her senses, she cried as she laughed. She personally buried the empty coffin again and brought her people back to the capital. She flipped the entire Chengchao Palace upside down first. She thought that Qi Yan might have had some troubles that she could not say, and that she might have left clues for her to find. But the result disappointed her.

Nangong Jingnü was somewhat upset, but she considered again: based on Qi Yan’s intellect, she could have made a perfect escape. Why would she leave an empty coffin behind?

That was the biggest clue left for her, wasn’t it?

Nangong Jingnü got herself back together. She swiftly assigned a few great officials to assist in politics and handed the power to govern the kingdom to the Crown Prince. She ordered people to make a copy of the map of the universe around the nine provinces and set off with her people.

Nangong Jingnü had considered putting up posters to search for someone with unusual eyes, but she realized that it might provoke Qi Yan, who’s mind worked beyond her grasp. What if she frightened her away and made her hide in the deep mountains instead? Wouldn’t she have just made things harder for herself?

But how could it be easy to find one person in a sea of people? Let alone to search secretly?

Nangong Jingnü would often race madly to a place because of one poem that was similar to Qi Yan’s literary style. She would carry immeasurable anticipation as she sought out a meeting with a gift prepared, but all she got in return was disappointment after disappointment.

This process could be summed up within a few sparse sentences, but the hardship within it could only be understood by the one who experienced it.

In the turn of an eye, Qi Yan and Ding You have already moved into Guang fishing village for six years. Qi Yan managed to gain a steady standing in the private school too.

Qi Yan was an outsider, and she had a solitary personality too. She was not like Ding You who was equipped with excellent medical skills. In the eyes of outsiders, Qi Yan did not go out to net fish in the sea, and she did not tend to any crops. How often do you see a thirty-something year old big man who lives like a lady and stays inside all day? Qi Yan also had a very tender face; not even the ladies in the village were as fair and pretty as her. But ‘pretty’ was not a good description for men at all.

If it wasn’t because the entire village relied on Ding You’s medical skills, Li Zheng would not have allowed Qi Yan to teach in the private school. Li Zheng simply allowed Qi Yan to teach calligraphy to children who had just started schooling as a favor for Ding You.

There was no greeting gift, but Qi Yan would be provided with a filling lunch every day. She would also get to receive two fresh fish and ten dried ones at the end of each month. Even though the villagers felt that this ‘mister Qi’ was not worth such a cost at all, doctor ‘Qi’ cared for his younger cousin very much. Hence they guessed it was still fine to give up some things to raise an idler for his sake.

More than a few matchmakers came to Ding You’s door once he had a well-known reputation, but Ding You rejected all them.

Ding You said that his younger cousin is a pitiful person, she does not have the strength to bind a chicken or any sort of survival skills. If he married someone, they would have to live separately. He was worried that Qi Yan would starve to death if she lived on her own.

Hearing that from Ding You, the villagers shunned Qi Yan even more now.

However, Qi Yan gave the entire village an enormous surprise. No one could have expected that: this weird outsider could actually write excellent calligraphy. Even the principal who was in his sixties was ashamed of his own inferiority.

Though Guang fishing village was a secluded place, it had no lack of people with good taste. Gradually, people started to request written works at her door. Qi Yan never rejected them, though she never conversed with anyone. As long as someone came to her door with a request, Qi Yan would silently accept the piece of paper that they presented. She would shut the door, then a written script would be slipped through the door’s edge a short moment later.

An elder of a certain family in the village mailed Qi Yan’s script to a junior who worked as an official in the Jian province. That junior gave Qi Yan’s writing an extremely high appraisal. He took a boat back to his hometown and he rode in a sedan to grant an interview to Qi Yan.

There were also some young men who had looser ideas. Once they had gotten Qi Yan’s scripts, they sailed to a certain bookstore in the Jian province for the monthly fair. One poetic couplet was actually sold for three liangs of fine silver!

Three liangs of fine silver! They wouldn’t have earned that much money even if they sold a boat full of fish!

Qi Yan’s reputation exploded overnight. Her popularity had actually surpassed Ding You who was known as a miracle doctor!

But this matter was a ‘secret’. A secret that the entire village knew about, all except for Ding You and Qi Yan.

The villagers were worried that Qi Yan would leave this place if she learned about her worth, hence the entire village tacitly acted as if nothing had changed.

Though, someone would knock on her door every once in a while to offer grain and live fish in exchange for a script, then they would sell it during the monthly fair.

Flashy white silver entered their pouches. Plenty of people built new houses. All except for Qi Yan and Ding You, who still lived in thatched huts, benefiting the village while they lived in poverty.

Later on, matchmakers started to go to Qi Yan’s home, but they were all rejected outside the door.

One day, after Qi Yan had left to teach at the private school in the morning, a horse carriage stopped before Qi Yan and Ding You’s gate…

There were up to a hundred people in the mighty formation, followed by two county officials. The villagers who wanted to spectate hid away once the county officials shouted at them.

To the villagers of Guang fishing village, a big old official was a god-like existence, while a county official was already a very major official.

The two county officials did not know who was inside the carriage, but their superior had fallen to his knees in terror once he saw the person inside. It seems like that person was a big official from the capital!

Those two county officials stood next to the horse carriage with the utmost deference. The carriage door opened, then Gu Rolan and Qiuju got down first to stand next to the carriage. After that, out came the true master…

Nangong Jingnü was dressed in casual clothes with a light veil covering her face. Though it was the simplest outfit, it appeared unspeakably expensive to the county officials.

Nangong Jingnü took out a piece of paper from her sleeve and asked, “The person who wrote this script stays here?”

The county official said, “Answering Sir, it is, according to the villagers.”

Nangong Jingnü’s fine brows knitted slightly as she looked at the two thatched huts. She did not like the sensation in her heart: even if she had gotten sick of a big courtyard in the imperial palace, she should at least stay in a proper courtyard. How could she stay in such a broken and old thatched hut?

The writing of the hermit shepherd was a rarer find than a thousand gold. Even when so many years had passed, it would have a price that reached the heavens in the capital. Even a copy would sell for a few hundred liangs of silver; how could an authentic work be sold for three to five liangs?

Hearing voices, Ding You pushed the door open and took a step outside. He froze on the spot. He opened his mouth a little, then kneeled on the ground dejectedly.

Nangong Jingnü’s heart finally landed on solid ground once she saw Ding You. She was so worked up that she wanted to cry, but she held it in since there were outsiders around: “The two of you have worked hard to lead the way, please return. Qiuju.”

Qiuju replied, “Understood, master.” Saying that, she took out two ingots of silver, then handed them to the county officials separately. Their eyes turned wide at once. They’ve worked in the government office for so many years, but other than the revenue silver they had to pay to the court, they have never seen such big pieces of silver before!

The county officials expressed their thanks profusely and backed away as they bowed.

Nangong Jingnü said, “Qiuju and Rolan are to stay, the rest must take a hundred steps back. Seal off this area.”

The guards cried, “Understood!”

Nangong Jingnü came up to Ding You. “Do you still recognize me?”

Ding You was silent for a moment and knocked his head to the ground. “This criminal Ding You greets your Majesty.”

Nangong Jingnü asked, “Where is she?”

Ding You replied, “Teaching in the private school.”

Nangong Jingnü was taken aback. She was so mad that it felt funny.

This person had tormented her to the point where death would be a relief, while she escaped to the edge of the world to live as neighbors with her old friend, and she had actually started to teach and guide others?

Nangong Jingnü’s teeth ached from resentment. She wished that she could see Qi Yan right now, so that she could pry her heart open and take a good look at what it was made of!

She wanted to ask her properly, just how could someone who had abandoned her home and wife be a model of virtue for others!

Nangong Jingnü said, “Take me to her, right now.”

Ding You straightened his back and he said quietly, “Your Majesty shouldn’t waste your effort. Qi Yan doesn’t remember anything anymore.”

Nangong Jingnü narrowed her phoenix eyes, and she emitted the intent to kill. “Ding You, do you still remember what I had said to you that day?”

Ding You gave a bitter laugh. “Your Majesty said that if this subject dared to lie to you, this subject’s corpse would be torn into a thousand pieces.”

Nangong Jingnü said, “As long as you remember it. Take me to her now if you still want to live!”

Ding You said, “Your Majesty has found this place through a thousand mile journey. Could your Majesty allow for a moment more? If your Majesty could dismiss the others and hear the whole story from this subject…”

“The two of you may go too.”

Nangong Jingnü said, “Stand up and answer.”

Ding You replied, “Understood.”

Ding You moved a stool over for Nangong Jingnü. “The story is too long, may your Majesty have a seat as you listen.”

After that, Ding You told Nangong Jingnü about the whole story. Including the numerous lapses of memory loss that Qi Yan had in the imperial palace.

Although Ding You had always carried a certain hope towards Qi Yan, the past six years of coexistence made Ding You understand: it doesn’t matter if Nangong Jingnü was in Qi Yan’s life or not. There was no chance for him.

To be with Qi Yan… That had always been a dream of King Xiang, for the goddess with no heart.

In the moment that Ding You saw Nangong Jingnü, he finally understood something that Qi Yan had told him in the past.

Qi Yan said, “Be it men or women… This heart of mine can’t keep anyone else for this life and this world.”

Ding You heard the sound of weeping. When he returned to his senses, he saw Nangong Jingnü’s tear streaked face. “The fire toad can only be found in Chiongtai. Once the fire toad is taken away from here, it would die and lose its effectiveness. This subject had to bring Qi Yan here to cure her condition, but she had forgotten your Majesty and everything that had happened before. I made up a random identity for her, and she believed it just like that. For the past three years that we were here, Qi Yan hardly ever stepped out of the door. She would gaze at your Majesty’s portrait in a trance all day. The only time that she initiated conversation with me was to ask where that painting came from. I lied to her by saying that it was just a dream she had, and she believed it too. Perhaps… She still remembers your Majesty in the depths of her heart.”

Nangong Jingnü wiped her tears away. The resentment in her heart was mostly gone, while heartache and regret filled it up instead.

Nangong Jingnü asked, “How has she been for the past few years? Is her health better now?”

Ding You replied, “The water condition in her body has already been dispelled. As for her life… Your Majesty could see it too.”

Ding You said, “It was my idea for her to teach in the private school. I was worried that she would eventually get sick if she stayed shut inside the house all day.”

Nangong Jingnü asked, “She still remembers the things that she had learned in the past?”

“Other than forgetting past experiences and becoming quiet, everything else is fine with her. Though, Qi Yan was pretty much like this when she was in the nameless valley. Perhaps this is how she actually is.”

“Take me to her.”

Ding You took a look at the sky and he answered, “Your Majesty should wait a while more. The private school only teaches for half a day, Qi Yan should be back after lunch.”

Nangong Jingnü entered Qi Yan’s house on her own. It was very dim inside the house. The smell of straw and mud filled the air.

The furnishing inside the room was very simple. There was one wooden bed, one table and one chair. An oil lamp was placed on the table, along with poor-quality inkstone, a few pieces of yellowish coarse paper, and one brush with falling hairs. A few sets of washed-out clothes were stacked neatly on the trunk at the foot of the bed. A broom leaned on a corner of the wall…

Nangong Jingnü felt a lump in her throat as she looked around. This was the place that her beloved person had lived in for six years…

Qi Yan’s departure caused Nangong Jingnü to lock her heart in a cage, but Qi Yan had imprisoned herself in a cage entirely.

This environment was even poorer than the rooms of the Supreme Court prison. Nangong Jingnü could not imagine how Qi Yan had spent her days here for the past six years.

Nangong Jingnü’s gaze landed on a painted scroll that hung on the wall. Seeing her painted self, Nangong Jingnü was caught in a momentary trance.

She was very young in her portrait. She held a smile in her lips and sentiment in her eyes. Nangong Jingnü could not quite remember herself like that anymore.

Qi Yan got off school and walked on the road back home with a scholar’s trunk on her back. Along the way, plenty of villagers gathered in groups of two and threes as they pointed towards her.

Qi Yan continued to walk in the direction home as she looked steadily forward. Once she was nearly there, she saw a hundred guards surrounding her courtyard. Qi Yan licked her lips nervously. Her hands tightened repeatedly around the band of her trunk.

The guards gave a courtesy with their eyes towards Qi Yan, while a lady flew up to her and called her “Da-ge”.

Qi Yan frowned and pressed her lips into a straight line. She was somewhat bewildered, hence she tilted away and dodged her.

Qiuju ran quickly to the house to report to Nangong Jingnü, who was both delighted and nervous to hear of Qi Yan’s return.

Nangong Jingnü wiped her tears dry and she went up to the door.

As Qi Yan was startled by Gu Rolan, she paced quickly back to her courtyard with a pale face. Nangong Jingnü pushed the door open and they nearly bumped into each other.

Qi Yan instinctively wanted to run, but when she saw that the person in the painting was actually right before her, she was stunned on the spot.

Qiuju said, “Please excuse this maid.”

Nangong Jingnü gazed at Qi Yan. As she looked at the person who had only appeared in her dreams for the past six years, she could not contain herself any longer. She spread her arms and pounced on Qi Yan.

Qi Yan was utterly against physical contact ever since she had lost her memories. Not even Ding You could touch her. But this time… Qi Yan did not escape from it.

Nangong Jingnü hugged Qi Yan tightly, as if Qi Yan might disappear if she let go.

Qi Yan instinctively took half a step back, but she was hugged too tightly; she could not budge at all.

Qi Yan replied, “Miss, what are you…”

Nangong Jingnü’s heart jerked. It was different to hear something from others than to experience it in person.

Truly hearing no recognition from Qi Yan at all, the pain in her heart felt a thousand times stronger than before. But Nangong Jingnü already felt extremely fortunate to be able to find her, and to hug her. She took a deep breath, then said firmly, “I’m never ever letting you leave me again.”

Qi Yan moved around a little. A peculiar feeling filled her heart. “Can you let go of this one first?”

Nangong Jingnü wanted to act spoiled and just say that she wouldn't, but she feared that it would frighten Qi Yan. The loss outweighed the gains, hence she let go in resignation.

But when Nangong Jingnü raised her head to look at Qi Yan, light suddenly filled her eyes. Nangong Jingnü caressed Qi Yan’s cheek, gently brushing away a clear drop on it with her thumb: “What are you crying for?” Her voice was extremely gentle, as if it was a whisper to her lover in the night.

Qi Yan raised her hand to feel a corner of her eye. She was stunned to sense the slight dampness on it.

Nangong Jingnü held Qi Yan’s hand. “You’ve forgotten, but I remember everything… Don’t reject me, alright? I won’t harm you ever again.”

Qi Yan felt rather dizzy. She who was usually against physical contact did not break free for the second time. Perhaps it was because of the painting that she had looked at for six years, or perhaps it was because of a certain voice in the depths of her heart. Qi Yan gave a very quiet “Mm”.

Nangong Jingnü gave a beautiful smile and embraced Qi Yan again.

Qi Yan’s face was somewhat red. She stood on the spot like a pillar for a very long while before she asked, “Miss, who are you?”

Nangong Jingnü said, “I’m called Nangong Jingnü, your legally wedded wife.”

Once her words landed, Qi Yan felt a pang in her mind. Countless images flashed before her: in a pitch-black night, her hand was joined with this lady who was hugging her as they walked through countless unfamiliar roads.

A sense of ease that she had not felt for a long time filled her heart. Qi Yan hugged Nangong Jingnü in return.

At this moment, Qi Yan still did not know what past she had with this woman in her arms. But this reunion had made an opening in her memories that were shut away for six years.

On a certain day in the future, Qi Yan would definitely remember.

‘The future’ may be expected soon. It was not actually far away.

The water condition had been solved. The rivers and mountains had been passed on. They still have a long, long time ahead of them.
